title: One content stream, two agent identities: “Instagram Agent” and “Social posts (IG/TikTok)” run side by side
surface: Calendar, Jobs, run history — everywhere runs are labelled
whatYouSee: On the calendar, 27 Jul stacks an "Instagram Agent" run chip directly above a "Social posts (IG/TikTok)" post chip; 21 Jul shows "TikTok Agent" twice from two different systems. The agents page sells "Instagram Agent"; deliverables and some runs are labelled "Social posts". On the call: "Why is it still social posts and Instagram agent is not the same? It's the same thing… this pisses me off."
whyItsWrong: The managed-product catalog (task_type social_post, name "Social posts") and the customAgents Instagram Agent are two identities for the same deliverable stream, so calendar, jobs and analytics double-report it and a client sees two agents where there is one. The team decided on the call to unify them.
evidence: customAgents collection — the Instagram Agent instance for the same client
src/components/run-calendar.tsx — chips render both identities on the same days
Team decision, portal review call 27 Jul 2026
fix: One identity per stream. Map task_type → the client's custom agent identity in a single shared label helper used by calendar, jobs, run history and analytics (the same helper fixes "TikTok Agent" duplicates); retire the client-facing "Social posts" catalog card for clients whose workspace has the Instagram agent. Cross-ref findings 39/45 — the managed products are already unrunnable from the UI, so nothing breaks.

title: The portal has no launch-vs-runs model — the architecture the team decided on has nowhere to live
surface: AI Agents (/clients/[id]/agents) — agent cards, schedule dialog, feedback
whatYouSee: Every agent card offers exactly two verbs: "Run now" and "Set schedule". There is no launch step that produces the template set, no template list on the card, no per-template run or feedback, no way to reorder the calendar's templates or leave a note for run day. The call spec'd all of it: launch = a setup run producing research + 3–5 templates, CTAs and goals; runs = day-of generation; feedback at the global level or per template; 25 credits to run one template on demand; clients reorder the calendar and drop notes the engine reads when it runs.
whyItsWrong: The data layer is already half-way there — every post is stamped with templateKey/templateName ("By The Numbers", …) — but no UI groups by template, so the concept the team is selling ("give feedback to this format" / "run this format now") has no surface. It also blocks the cost split the call asked for: launch cost vs recurring run cost cannot be separated when both are just "a run".
evidence: src/lib/types.ts:449–456 — templateKey/templateName exist on posts and are rendered nowhere as a group
src/lib/custom-agent-launch.ts — a guided run brief, not a launch lifecycle
src/components/schedule-run-modal.tsx — one "Ongoing direction" textarea, no templates
Feedback actions are per-draft only (x/li/reddit draft feedback) — no template or agent-level target
Team decision, portal review call 27 Jul 2026
fix: Add a launch state and a per-client template registry to the agent instance: the launch run persists its templates; the card renders them with per-template Run (25 credits) and per-template feedback; a second feedback control targets the whole agent; calendar slots reference a templateKey plus an optional client note consumed at run time; analytics tag runs launch vs recurring. This is the biggest single work item in the document — it is the product model, not a patch.
